info.name: CloneInsta API v1
info.description:
Import this collection after starting PostgreSQL and Mailpit, applying migrations, and running `npm run dev:server`. The REST base URL is `{{baseUrl}}`; protected requests require `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`. New registrations are `PENDING_VERIFICATION` and cannot log in until confirmed. To exercise M11B locally, set `verificationEmail` to a new unused address, run **Auth / Register**, open the local Mailpit UI at `http://localhost:8025`, copy the email link's `token` query value into `verificationToken`, then run **Auth / Confirm email verification**. The M11B link targets `PUBLIC_APP_URL/verify-email`, but no browser verification page exists yet.

Run **Auth / Login as demo user** for normal protected calls: its test script stores the returned access token. Login also sets the HttpOnly refresh cookie and readable `cloneinsta_csrf` cookie. Before Refresh or Logout, copy that cookie value into `csrfToken` if Postman did not populate it automatically; those two endpoints require the cookie plus `Origin: http://localhost:5173` and `X-CSRF-Token: {{csrfToken}}`.

Seed credentials: `alice_demo` / `UserDemo123!`, `bob_demo` / `UserDemo123!`, and `admin_demo` / `AdminDemo123!`. Use Alice for normal-user requests and log in as Admin for the Admin folder. The values in `userId`, `postId`, `commentId`, `conversationId`, `messageId`, and `reportId` are placeholders: copy IDs from a successful previous response. Cursor values are opaque base64url strings returned in `pageInfo.nextCursor`; never construct them manually.

Every successful payload includes `requestId`. Errors follow `{ error: { code, message }, requestId }`; validation errors also include `error.details`. Representative successful response shapes: verification request `{ message, requestId }`; verification confirm `{ user, requestId }`; login `{ accessToken, user, requestId }`; feed `{ posts, pageInfo, requestId }`; report `{ report, requestId }`; conversation list `{ conversations, pageInfo, requestId }`. All non-auth data routes are versioned below `/api/v1`. Socket.IO realtime events (conversation/message sync, send and read) are intentionally not included because this is a REST Postman collection.

request.description: Checks the Express service and Prisma/PostgreSQL readiness. 200 example: `{ status: "ok", database: "up", service: "cloneinsta-server", environment, timestamp, requestId }`.

Creates a `PENDING_VERIFICATION` user and sends its 24-hour one-time verification message to local Mailpit. It does not issue access/refresh tokens. Set `verificationEmail` to a new unused address before retrying. Username is lowercased and must be 3-30 lowercase letters, numbers, dots, or underscores; password is 8-72 chars with lowercase, uppercase, and a number. 201 example: `{ user: { id, username, displayName, email, role, status: "PENDING_VERIFICATION", emailVerifiedAt: null, createdAt }, requestId }`.

Sends a replacement verification message only when `verificationEmail` belongs to a pending account, but always returns the same 202 body for pending, unknown, and active addresses to avoid account enumeration. A replacement consumes older unused verification tokens. Limited to 3 requests per 15 minutes per email and IP; exceeding the limit returns `429 AUTH_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_RATE_LIMITED`.

Copy `token` from the local Mailpit email link into `verificationToken`. A valid token is one-time, expires after 24 hours, and atomically activates the pending account. 200 example: `{ user: { status: "ACTIVE", emailVerifiedAt }, requestId }`. Invalid, expired, or reused tokens return `400 AUTH_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED`; confirmations are limited to 10 per 15 minutes per IP.

exec: pm.test('returns an access token', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Uses a seeded normal user and stores `accessToken`. Postman keeps the refresh and CSRF cookies for localhost. 200 example: `{ accessToken, user, requestId }`.

exec: pm.test('returns an admin access token', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Run before Admin requests. It replaces `accessToken` with an ADMIN token.

Requires the refresh-cookie session, exact local client Origin, and matching CSRF cookie/header pair. It rotates the refresh token. 200 example: `{ accessToken, user, requestId }`. A missing or mismatched CSRF header returns `CSRF_INVALID`.
Requires the same cookie/Origin/CSRF checks as Refresh. Revokes the current refresh session and clears auth cookies. Success is `204 No Content` (there is no JSON body).
Returns the authenticated user's safe profile DTO and relation counts. 200 example: `{ profile, requestId }`.
Updates only the authenticated profile. At least one allowed field is required; blank bio/avatar normalize to null. 200 example: `{ profile, requestId }`.

Searches ACTIVE users by username/display name. `limit` is 1-20 (default 10); pass the opaque `pageInfo.nextCursor` to get the next page. 200 example: `{ users: [], pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`.
Idempotently follows `userId`; self-follow is rejected. 200 example: `{ following: true, requestId }`.
Idempotently removes the current viewer's follow relation. 200 example: `{ following: false, requestId }`.

Idempotently blocks the target and writes an audit record only for a real state change. A block hides that pair from direct-message lookup, creation, read, send, and realtime bootstrap. 200 example: `{ blocked: true, requestId }`.
Idempotently unblocks the target. Existing historic messages remain retained for audit. 200 example: `{ blocked: false, requestId }`.
Gets the stable cursor-paginated feed. `limit` is 1-20 (default 10); use a returned opaque cursor for the next request. 200 example: `{ posts: [], pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`.
Lists the current user's visible posts. 200 example: `{ posts: [], requestId }`.
Returns one visible post with the safe detail DTO. 200 example: `{ post, requestId }`.

Send `multipart/form-data`; do not manually set the Content-Type boundary. `image` is required and is validated for size, MIME/magic bytes, dimensions, and generated storage filename. `caption` is optional and at most 2200 chars. 201 example: `{ post, requestId }`.
Idempotently likes a visible post. 200 example: `{ liked: true, likeCount, requestId }`.
Idempotently removes the current viewer's like. 200 example: `{ liked: false, likeCount, requestId }`.
Soft-deletes a post when the caller is its owner or an admin. 200 example: `{ deletedPostId, requestId }`.
Creates a 1-1000 character comment on a visible post. 201 example: `{ comment, requestId }`.
Deletes a comment when the caller owns the comment, owns its post, or is an admin. 200 example: `{ deletedCommentId, requestId }`.

Creates a report for exactly one target: use one of `reportedUserId`, `reportedPostId`, or `reportedCommentId`, never two. Supported reasons: SPAM, HARASSMENT, HATE_SPEECH, VIOLENCE, NUDITY, SELF_HARM, IMPERSONATION, MISINFORMATION, OTHER. A real `REPORT_CREATED` audit record is written atomically with safe metadata only (reason, target id/type); direct-message content is not copied. 201 example: `{ report, requestId }`.
Alternative exactly-one-target report request. 201 example: `{ report, requestId }`.
Alternative exactly-one-target report request. 201 example: `{ report, requestId }`.

ADMIN only. Lists reports using status `PENDING|RESOLVED|DISMISSED`, sort `newest|oldest`, limit 1-20, and opaque cursor pagination. 200 example: `{ reports: [], pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`. A normal token returns `FORBIDDEN`.
ADMIN only. Dismisses the report; `note` is optional but, when provided, must be 1-500 chars. 200 example: `{ report, requestId }`.
ADMIN only. Hides the post/comment target and resolves the report. A nonblank 1-500 character audit note is required. 200 example: `{ report, requestId }`.
ADMIN only. Bans the reported USER target and resolves the report; a nonblank 1-500 character audit note is required. 200 example: `{ report, requestId }`.

ADMIN only. Filters by optional `action`, `actorId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, ISO datetimes `from`/`to`, `sort`, `limit` 1-50, and cursor. 200 example: `{ auditLogs: [], pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`. Metadata is deliberately safe and omits secrets/tokens/private message content.

Lists accepted direct-message conversations for the current viewer. `folder` is `inbox|requests`; default inbox. `limit` is 1-20, default 20. 200 example: `{ conversations: [], pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`.
Lists pending direct-message requests for the current recipient. Request conversations cannot be replied to until accepted. 200 example: `{ conversations: [], pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`.

Creates a direct thread or returns the existing one. A newly initiated contact can appear as a request for its recipient. Blocked pairs are intentionally hidden rather than exposing block state. 201 for a new conversation, 200 for reuse; both return `{ conversation, requestId }`.

Participant-only thread lookup with 1-20 message cursor pagination. 200 example: `{ conversation, messages: [], readState, pageInfo: { nextCursor }, requestId }`. Nonparticipants and blocked pairs do not gain thread access.

Participant-only REST send, content 1-2000 chars. Pending requests cannot be answered until accepted; pair blocks also prevent sends. Sender burst protection can return `429 MESSAGE_RATE_LIMITED`. 201 example: `{ message, requestId }`.
Marks messages through the supplied visible message ID as read for the current participant. 200 example: `{ readState, requestId }`.
Recipient-only action for a pending request. It moves the thread into Inbox and enables normal sending. 200 example: `{ conversation, requestId }`; the action creates a safe audit event.

Recipient-only action for a pending request. It hides the request for that recipient while retaining minimal safe audit history. A later peer message may create a new request. 200 example: `{ conversationId, requestId }`.
